record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For every connected graph G on n at least 3 vertices, is the spectral spread s(G) = λ1(G) − λn(G) always at most sqrt(4qn − 3q^2 − 2q + 1), where q = floor(2n/3) and λ1(G), λn(G) are the largest and smallest adjacency eigenvalues of G? Equivalently, is the maximum spectral spread among connected n-vertex graphs attained exactly by the complete split graph CS(n,q), meaning a graph consisting of a q-vertex clique and an independent set on the remaining n−q vertices with every clique vertex adjacent to every independent-set vertex, with independent-set size ceil(n/3)?

evidence.quote: The problem of finding the maximum value of s(G) among the class of connected graphs of given order n is an open problem. Experiments done with the AutoGraphiX system led to the following conjecture. Conjecture 3.1... Given n, the maximal value of the spectral spread of a graph on n vertices is obtained for a complete split graph CS(n,q) with an independent set of size n-q = ⌈n/3⌉.

Now, we reformulate Conjecture 3.1 in order to provide an upper bound in addition to extremal graphs. Conjecture 3.1’... Let G be a connected graph on n ≥ 3 vertices. Then s(G) ≤ sqrt(4 q n - 3 q^2 - 2 q + 1) with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n,q) with an independent set of size n-q = ⌈n/3⌉ and a clique of size q = ⌊2n/3⌋.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple connected graph on n ≥ 3 vertices, with adjacency matrix A(G) and real eigenvalues λ1(G) ≥ λ2(G) ≥ … ≥ λn(G). Define the spectral spread of G by s(G) = λ1(G) − λn(G). For integers n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ q ≤ n−1, let CS(n, q) denote the complete split graph consisting of a clique on q vertices and an independent set on the remaining n − q vertices, with every vertex of the clique adjacent to every vertex of the independent set. Let q = ⌊2n/3⌋, so that n − q = ⌈n/3⌉.

Prove or disprove: for every connected graph G on n ≥ 3 vertices,
  s(G) ≤ √(4qn − 3q² − 2q + 1),
with equality if and only if G ≅ CS(n, q). Equivalently, show that the maximum of s(G) over all connected graphs on n vertices is attained exactly by the complete split graph CS(n, ⌊2n/3⌋).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originally due to Gregory–Hershkowitz–Kirkland and rediscovered/refined via AutoGraphiX experiments) that the spread-maximizing connected graph on n vertices is the complete split graph CS(n, ⌊2n/3⌋) was proved for all sufficiently large n by Breen, Riasanovsky, Tait and Urschel using graph limits and numerical analysis. The statement is not yet known to hold for all n ≥ 3, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Maximum spread of graphs and bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A pair of 20-year-old conjectures of Gregory, Hershkowitz, and Kirkland regarding the spread of graphs ... proven for all n sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: The spread conjecture (extremal graph is the join of a clique of size ⌊2n/3⌋ and an independent set of size ⌈n/3⌉) is resolved for all sufficiently large n.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory
status_evidence.snippet: The maximum spread is (asymptotically) achieved by a split graph ...
status_evidence.claim: The result is stated as an asymptotic/large-n theorem, with the general-n statement listed among related open problems.
